stop_if: A claim is corrected in some of the files or records that repeat it without a whole-tree grep for every phrasing of the claim being run FIRST, its results written down as a list, and the actual edits checked against that list afterward. This is now the FOURTH consecutive incomplete multi-location correction in this package alone - WP-115 twice before it, `badf/current-state.json`'s `active_work_package.objective` in fix round 2 (found only because `git diff 6b81703..4f21ef7 -- badf/current-state.json` was empty), and then a fourth instance inside fix round 1 itself: round 1 changed the GUARD's rule (removing the Windows-word requirement, going from three controls to four) and re-grepped for the RECORDS' claim that the machine's alias symptom had reproduced, but never re-grepped for every place that DESCRIBED the rule it had just changed - DEC-122's `decision` field and this checkpoint's own `completed[4]` and `recovery.stop_if[5]` all kept asserting the old, now-false rule (a literal `Windows` word requirement, three controls) until the final whole-branch review found it. THE ENUMERATION OWED WHEN A RULE CHANGES IS NOT THE SAME AS THE ENUMERATION OWED WHEN A FACTUAL CLAIM IS CORRECTED: a factual claim (the machine's alias state) is found by grepping for ITS phrasings; a RULE CHANGE (a guard's regex, a control's behaviour, a check's population) is found by grepping for every SENTENCE THAT DESCRIBES THE THING THAT CHANGED - the rule's name, its control count, its vocabulary - which is a different and easy-to-forget search because the changed code no longer contains the wrong description; only the records that talk ABOUT the code do. Enumerate before editing, every time: for a repeated claim, grep the claim's phrasings; for a changed rule, grep every description of the rule, not only the record that prompted the change.

THE GUARD HAS A FALSE-GREEN HOLE, FOUND BY THE FINAL WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW AND DECLARED RATHER THAN CHASED. tests/test_resume_protocol_command.py's property is 'some other interpreter token (`python` or `py`) on the same line as `python3`,' not 'a second, actually-runnable invocation is shown.' The sentence 'Run python3 -m unittest discover -s tests; any python interpreter of 3.11 or later will do' passes: the bare word `python` inside that prose satisfies the check even though no second command is ever shown. Verified directly against the module's own functions rather than assumed. Not fixed: every attempt in fix round 1 to require more structure (a specific vocabulary - the literal words `python` and `Windows`) traded this exact false-green for a false-red on legitimate content (the `py`/PowerShell rewrite), and a pattern strict enough to demand a backticked second command would likely do the same to some future, equally legitimate wording nobody has written yet. Widening the regex to chase this hole is exactly the mistake fix round 1 already made and corrected once; declaring the hole is the safer choice, and AGENTS.md section 3's own human review is what actually keeps its prose honest against this specific gap.
